exposure: maternal factors (assisted reproduction, pregnancy plurality, maternal age)
perinatal factors (mode of birth, gestational age at birth)
neonatal care practices (NICU care, parental involvement during NICU hospitalization, Kangaroo mother care, breastfeeding practices)
post-discharge support (level of follow-up care, access to supportive therapies like physiotherapy and RSV prophylaxis, parental awareness and use of national initiatives)
outcome: short- and long-term evolution of preterm infants
enrollment rates in structured follow-up programs
reliance on private services for physical therapy
access to multidisciplinary follow-up and public physiotherapy
parental awareness and endorsement of national initiatives
cohort: The study included 360 mothers of preterm infants born between 2001 and 2025 in Romania.
finding: The study revealed that only 25% of preterm infants were enrolled in structured follow-up programs, with many families relying on private services for physical therapy, indicating significant gaps in public post-discharge support.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with lower gestational age at birth.
cross-section timing: Data was collected around 2025, gathering information on infants born between 2001 and 2025, thus reflecting their status at various points up to 24 years post-birth.
